name: Amaze Holdings, Inc.

profile.description: Amaze Holdings (formerly Fresh Vine Wine, renamed March 2025) runs a creator-commerce platform that lets social-media creators sell merchandise and products through storefronts, with a reported 13-15 million creator stores [2][3]. NYSE American started delisting proceedings on September 29, 2026 because of the stock's abnormally low price, and the stock was delisted effective October 12, 2026 and now trades OTC. This followed a 1-for-8 reverse split on July 24, 2026 [1]. Revenue was $1.97M in 2025, and the company had about $5.3M of notes payable and other debt as of September 30, 2026 [1][5].

innovation.label: WEAK
innovation.analysis: Track Record (0/3): The company's main change was a reverse-merger style pivot from Fresh Vine Wine into creator commerce. It has not produced a successful new revenue stream: 2025 revenue was $1.97M, and the stock ended up delisted from NYSE American [1][5]. AI Deployment (2/2): Amaze launched Amaze Commerce in March 2026, whose first capability, Moments AI, analyzes a creator's social profile and turns engaging content into products. It also rolled out AI-driven Brand Analysis, Trending Moments, and Suggested Themes tools to creators [2]. Market Share (0/2): Revenue of about $0.6M per quarter shows no share leadership in creator commerce despite millions of dormant storefronts [1][2]. Pipeline (1/2): A Demand-Side Platform and Creator Data Model launched in May 2026, but no future products with revenue visibility were named [2]. R&D Intensity (0/1): No reliable R&D disclosure was found in the fetched sources.

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (2/4): Amaze says it helps creators turn content into revenue. That is clear about whom it serves but generic for the creator-economy sector [2]. Community Impact (0/2): No charitable or community programs were found [4]. Employee Retention (0/2): The company has 28 employees and announced a leadership transition in which an interim CEO replaced Aaron Day, CEO since 2021. That signals instability, not retention [3][5]. Insider Buying (0/2): No net insider buying was found. Financing has instead come from dilutive issuance under an S-1 registration [1].

infrastructure.label: WEAK
infrastructure.analysis: HARD RULE — Liquidity Floor triggered. At a $0.0103 share price, even the 3-month average volume of 5.80M shares gives only about $60K of daily dollar volume. The 10-day average of 444,860 shares is about $4.6K per day. Both are far below the $1,000,000 threshold, so Infrastructure = 0 [5]. The underlying metrics are also weak: ROE of -145.7%, YoY revenue growth of -28.8%, and a market cap of about $0.37M. D/E of 65.8% is the only metric at target. Profit margin is shown as null because Yahoo reports 0.0% despite large net losses. The forward P/E of 0.04 is not meaningful and is excluded [5].

ai_resilience.label: HIGH RISK
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (3/9): Amaze's product is software and design tooling that helps creators make and sell merchandise. Generative AI design tools and the native commerce features of the large social and e-commerce platforms can replicate this cheaply, and Amaze has no physical, regulatory, or data moat at its revenue scale [2]. Its data on 15M+ creator stores is a modest asset, but most of those stores are inactive given quarterly revenue of about $0.6M [1][2]. AI Opportunity (0/1): Moments AI and related tools are shipping, but the company reports no revenue figure attributable to them [2].

infinite_game.summary: Amaze is in survival mode. It has been delisted to OTC, done a reverse split, faced a going-concern history, changed leadership, and lost a $1.3M court judgment, all of which leave no room for long-term play [1][3][4]. Sinek would see a company whose decisions are driven by the next financing and listing deadline rather than a cause [1].

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (1/3): 'Empowering creators to turn content into revenue' points at an outside group, but it is the standard pitch of every creator-economy platform. It has not been tested over time, since the current business identity dates only to the 2025 rename [2][5].

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (0/2): The company has 28 employees, a CEO transition to an interim leader, a going-concern paragraph on its 2024 audit, and an exchange delisting. This is organizational instability in which people protect themselves rather than advance a cause [3][4][5].

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): No management commentary was found that acknowledges competitors such as Shopify, TikTok Shop, or Printful as benchmarks for improvement. Messaging focuses on its own platform's AI features [2].

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): The company abandoned its wine business identity to become a creator-commerce platform and launched a new 'operating system' (Amaze Commerce) in 2026 [2][5]. These moves were driven by desperation rather than a Just Cause and have not yet succeeded, so they earn only partial credit.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (0/2): Recent decisions were reactive. These include a reverse split after an NYSE trading halt, a decision not to appeal the delisting, and dilutive financing [1]. There is no example of sacrificing near-term results for long-term capability.

investment_thesis: The only bull case is an option-value bet. Amaze has a large creator footprint (a reported 13-15 million storefronts) and launched AI tools in 2026 (Moments AI, Demand-Side Platform, Creator Data Model). The company said Q2 2026 revenue grew about 32% sequentially to about $0.6M, with sequential improvement in margin and net loss [1][2]. If the AI tools reactivate dormant creators at scale, revenue could grow from a very low base.
thesis_continued: The bear case dominates. The stock was delisted from NYSE American effective October 12, 2026 after an abnormally-low-price trading halt and a 1-for-8 reverse split, and it now trades OTC at about $0.01 with a market cap of about $0.37M [1][5]. Revenue is tiny ($1.97M in 2025; Q2 2026 down 28.8% YoY), ROE is -145.7%, and notes payable and other debt total about $5.3M against minimal cash generation [1][5]. A Kentucky court awarded G&I IX Aviation about $1.31M against a subsidiary (under appeal), and the 2024 audit included a going-concern paragraph [4]. Daily dollar volume is far below IOWN's $1M liquidity floor, so the stock cannot be traded at portfolio scale [5].
key_catalysts: Monetization of Moments AI and the May 2026 Demand-Side Platform across the 15M+ creator-store base, which would show up as consecutive quarters of sequential revenue growth above the ~$0.6M Q2 2026 level [1][2]
A successful appeal of the ~$1.31M G&I IX Aviation judgment, removing a claim equal to more than half of 2025 revenue [4]
Financing or a strategic transaction that addresses the ~$5.3M of notes payable and other debt [1]
key_risks: Insolvency or further heavy dilution: ~$5.3M of debt, a going-concern history, and dependence on S-1 equity raises at a $0.01 share price [1][4]
Illiquidity and reduced disclosure after the OTC move; daily dollar volume of about $5K-60K is far below institutional thresholds [1][5]
Competitive and AI commoditization from platform-native commerce (TikTok Shop, Instagram, Shopify) and generative design tools that make Amaze's creator tooling easy to replace [2]
